This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 38 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `33c47902d66a8d440cfc535cd11e1c4739078245` — the merge of head `3bbff329c32ed91ef4bee9392f362449ecd74f8e` into base `959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 33c47902d66a8d440cfc535cd11e1c4739078245 && git checkout 33c47902d66a8d440cfc535cd11e1c4739078245
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678 3bbff329c32ed91ef4bee9392f362449ecd74f8e && git checkout -B drift-repro 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678 && git merge --no-ff 3bbff329c32ed91ef4bee9392f362449ecd74f8e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 959c209d56a8b9ab6f7e561e87700721194e4678` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `90bb6549a87ef271f7f895eaf80a9359027f9f0e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22074 (body; comments 6038422460 triage ruling, 6050889097 claim, 6051891554 os-dev-report), PR #22173 (body, 18-file list, net diff against the merge-base 033e5c53: 8 commits, +664/-26), and the check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-08T04:14Z. Base-tree facts below are read from the clone at that merge-base and from the head's blobs; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface, plugin-auth (widening).** The root entry gains `createIdentityObjectsPlugin`, `IdentityObjectsPlugin`, `IdentityObjectsPluginOptions` and `IDENTITY_OBJECTS_PLUGIN_NAME` through `export *` of the new module; no name collides with an existing export, and `package.json` exports are unchanged (`.` and `./rate-limit-storage`). RIGHT. `authIdentityManifest` stays in `manifest.ts`, which the index does not export, so the builder is not public. RIGHT.

**One list, one owner.** `authIdentityObjects` plus `authObjectExtensions` plus the header are the one builder; `AuthPlugin` spreads that builder into its single registration and nothing later in its literal re-sets `objects`, `objectExtensions` or `defaultDatasource` (the later keys are `pages`, `dashboards`, the SSO nav spread). Both paths register under `AUTH_PLUGIN_ID` = `com.objectstack.plugin-auth`, so the objects keep one owning package whichever plugin a kernel mounts (ADR-0029 D3, single owner per object); the kernel plugin name `com.objectstack.auth.identity-objects` is distinct only because the kernel keys plugins by name. RIGHT. plugin-security declares `AUTHZ_STORE_IDENTITY_OBJECTS = ['sys_user', 'sys_member']` and registers nothing; its `package.json` gains no plugin-auth dependency; the error names the package by string. RIGHT per the ruling's "declares, does not register".

**Accept-set narrowing, plugin-security.** The gate is a `kernel:ready` handler subscribed at the head of `start()`. Both kernels dispatch `kernel:ready` with `triggerHookOrThrow` (kernel-base.ts, the #5170 boot-gate contract), so the throw rejects `bootstrap()` on ObjectKernel and LiteKernel alike. RIGHT. It asks `ql.getSchema(name)`, which is `registry.getObject` on the same registry the read path's `find('sys_member')` consults, so the boot question is the read's question. RIGHT. Subscribed in `start()`, not `init()`: `composeForDeclarations` in schema-migrate.ts suppresses a host plugin's `start()` and the kernel still fires `kernel:ready`, so `os migrate` keeps booting; an `init()` subscription would have refused it. RIGHT. `PluginContext.hook` is typed, so the `(ctx as any).hook` cast under a `typeof` guard is unneeded, but it is the file's own convention (the ADR-0029 D8 i18n hook, `runBootstrap`), and a hook-less context exists only as a test double; every kernel context carries `hook`. Acceptable, named.

**Who is newly refused, read from every non-test `SecurityPlugin` composition on this tree.**
- `os serve` (cli `serve.ts`): the SecurityPlugin mount sits inside the same `else` branch as the AuthPlugin mount ("Pair:"); the host-kernel branch and the no-secret branch mount neither. Not refused. RIGHT.
- `@objectstack/verify` `bootStack` mounts `AuthPlugin` unconditionally (harness.ts, the `kernel.use(new AuthPlugin(...))` at the top level of the boot); `verify --rls` boots through `bootStack` with a `security:` override; every dogfood fixture is a `security:` override into `bootStack`. Not refused. RIGHT, and the card's measure-first is answered: verify is the sanctioned app-suite kit, the export still lands for kits that compose their own kernel.
- `check:app-nav-i18n` (lint.yml) calls `SecurityPlugin.start()` on a fake context whose `hook` is a no-op; nothing fires. Not refused.
- `DevPlugin`: `services.auth !== false` is the default, so the stock dev stack mounts `AuthPlugin`. `services: { auth: false }` with security left on, or plugin-auth not installed while plugin-security is, is newly refused: `DevPlugin.start()` hands the real context to `SecurityPlugin.start()` and `kernel:ready` fires after it. By code reading, as the dev says; see ③.
- In-repo harnesses: three went red and now mount the preset (runtime 1, service-automation 2); three plugin-security doubles that fire every `kernel:ready` handler now answer exactly the two names from `getSchema` and nothing else, so they do not widen what the double vouches for. RIGHT.

**Co-mount refusal.** `IdentityObjectsPlugin.init()` detects `AuthPlugin` through the presence of the `auth` service, which only `AuthPlugin.init()` registers in product code; `optionalDependencies: ['com.objectstack.auth']` orders that `init()` first (ADR-0116 order-if-present), so the proxy is sound for the real pair and pinned. A kit that stubs an `auth` service and also mounts the preset would be refused with a message naming `AuthPlugin`. Edge, named, non-blocking.

**Datasource.** The builder inherits the header's `defaultDatasource: 'cloud'` unless `manifestDatasource` is passed, exactly as `AuthPlugin` behaves today; pin 1 boots a SQLite `driver.default` kit on the default. Unchanged semantics, and the option is documented in the changeset. RIGHT.

**Cross-lane wiring.** service-automation's devDependency on plugin-auth creates no workspace cycle (plugin-auth's closure is core, platform-objects, rest, service-messaging, spec, types and the better-auth family; none reaches service-automation). The lockfile's three lines are one `workspace:*` link; no external package is newly resolved, so this diff adds no advisory. The anchored vitest alias follows the file's existing rows. RIGHT.

**Pins.** The four ruled pins are present: pin 1 with a manifest-registering app stand-in (runtime owns `AppPlugin` and depends on plugin-auth, so importing it here would be a workspace cycle; the stand-in does what `AppPlugin.init()` does) plus a control; pin 2 resolves grants from `sys_member`; pin 3 is refused by name and the message names the export; pin 4 pins `AuthPlugin`'s one registration `toBe` the same arrays. The plugin-security suite pins the refusal on a real kernel with a stand-in package, proving the gate asks the registry and not the registrar. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22074-auth-identity-objects-plugin.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` **minor**, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. New exports, nothing removed or renamed. Matches the diff. RIGHT.
- `.changeset/22074-security-identity-objects-boot-refusal.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security` **minor** with **BREAKING** stated, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention that `check-changeset-no-major` enforces. Matches the diff: a composition that booted is refused at boot. RIGHT. ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: no spec key, export, option or stored shape is removed, renamed or re-shaped, so no ledger entry can exist and the remedy is a kernel-composition edit; the marker closes the other five arms on facts. The right arm of the closed set. RIGHT. The remedy is carried in prose because the gate refuses a FROM-TO table under this arm. Carried.
- PR body `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the dominant arm and equals the dispatch's corrected line; each changeset carries exactly one arm; no `skip-changeset`. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (os-dev-report deviations, out-of-scope findings, PR acceptance notes), each answered:

1. Gate armed in `start()` rather than `init()`: answered above; right, and the host-composition test's continued green is the pin.
2. `auth-plugin.ts` import block edited beyond the :645 region: required by the builder; adjacent and minimal. Accepted.
3. Six cross-lane files: each is a harness that boots `SecurityPlugin` without `AuthPlugin`, or the dependency, alias and lockfile line those harnesses need; under the stop line and enumerated for the seat to declare. Accepted.
4. plugin-security remedy as prose: the gate's constraint under the chosen arm. Accepted.
5. Branch sits on 033e5c53 and `main` has moved since; the dev read none of the later commits touching a diff file, and CI's merge ref carries the joint check. The seat merges `main` before queueing if the queue asks. Accepted.
6. Commit trailer form: not a contract matter.
7. **`DevPlugin` with `services: { auth: false }` and security on (or plugin-auth absent) is newly refused at boot, by code reading only.** Within the ruling: "a kernel with plugin-security but without the identity objects fails at boot, with an error naming the missing objects and the plugin that registers them". The changeset's remedy holds by code reading: `extraPlugins` are pushed into `childPlugins` and `init()`-ed with the real context after the manifest service exists, and the gate runs at `kernel:ready` after `DevPlugin.start()`. Not run on this tree. **Escalated to the seat, non-blocking:** the dev marks it "carrier: none"; a published package's own composition that is newly refused should carry a plugin-dev follow-up card (DevPlugin composes `createIdentityObjectsPlugin()` itself in the auth-off, security-on branch, or its header documents the `extraPlugins` remedy), not only a changeset sentence.
8. A light subpath entry for the preset (the root entry evaluates better-auth): outside this card's fence; a devpath follow-up at the seat's discretion. Non-blocking.
9. `dispatch-gates` derived neither `check:init-service-contract` nor `check:startup-registry-verdict` for a diff editing plugin `init()`/`start()` and declarations, and the former caught a real defect when run by hand: carrier is the PM seat, as the dev routes it. Noted for the seat.
10. `AuthzIdentityObjectsMissingError` is `export class` in `security-plugin.ts` but not re-exported from plugin-security's index (which exports only `SecurityPlugin` from that module), so it is not a public export and consumers identify the refusal by `name` and `missingObjects`; the changeset's "an error named" is accurate. No widening arm is owed on plugin-security. Named; if the seat wants `instanceof` for consumers, that is a follow-up export, not a defect here.

`open_questions`: none.

Check-runs on the head at the reading above: `Validate Package Dependencies` is red with the base's own OSV matches on `next@16.3.6` (card #22148; red on `main`'s scheduled scan and on every dependency-touching PR until the lockfile fix lands); this PR's lockfile adds one workspace link and no resolved package, so the red is inherited, not added. `Console Pin Gate` and `Packed-tarball smoke` are skipped by design. Every other completed check is green; the still-running ones are not yet verdicts and the seat lands only on green.
